messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: stan::io::reader and stan::io::writer use
parts:
Do stan::io::reader and stan::io::writer get used anywhere besides
when the parser generates model::transform_inits? I’m planning
on cleaning these up in refactoring the var_contexts and don’t
want to have any unintended side effects.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan::io::reader and stan::io::writer use
parts:
The reader is used in

write_csv()
write_array()
log_prob()

Basically, everywhere you need to do the conversion from
unconstrained to constrained.

The writer is used in:

transform_inits()
write_csv_header()
write_csv()

In general, you can just look at a compiled model to see
where things get used. It's easier than tracing through the
code generator.

- Bob

> On Apr 2, 2015, at 2:01 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Do stan::io::reader and stan::io::writer get used anywhere besides
> when the parser generates model::transform_inits? I’m planning
> on cleaning these up in refactoring the var_contexts and don’t
> want to have any unintended side effects.
>

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan::io::reader and stan::io::writer use
parts:
The code generator's modular. All you need to do is remove
the function to write the CSVs. These are definitions of
generate_write_csv() and generate_write_csv_header(), along with
the calls to them in the generate_cpp() function.

- Bob
